svg.aria-label: B2-F04 — neither denser sampling nor quieter gauges change the answer
svg.desc: Two bar panels. The left panel shows the widest admissible run in log-10 cycles at 5, 10, 20 and 50 points per decade: 5 / decade reaches 0.000, 10 / decade reaches 0.000, 20 / decade reaches 0.100, 50 / decade reaches 0.100. Every bar falls short of the dashed rule at 1.0 cycle, so none certifies, and a tenfold increase in sampling density does not close the gap. The right panel shows the fraction of seeds returning INCONCLUSIVE at four noise levels: every bar is at 100 percent, σ = 0.1 psi answered 0 of 200, σ = 0.5 psi answered 0 of 200, σ = 2 psi answered 0 of 200, σ = 10 psi answered 0 of 200. Since the noise-free record already declines, this is the expected direction. The result worth recording is that no replicate produced a false acceptance either.

svg.text: One structural detail rather than a discovery about the physics: the rule needs 15 points inside a window of at least one decade, so 10 points per decade

svg.text: cannot certify a one-decade window at any duration. It would need 1.4 decades of flat derivative first.
